MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  DECEMBER 3, 2018

  A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
  order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chamber, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by CHAIR
  MEDAWAR.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER ZIGRANG led those in attendance in the Pledge of Allegiance

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Edler, Carman, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang,
  Schachter, Yoo

  STAFF PRESENT:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom,
  and Administrative Assistant Corea

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  SCOTT to,

  APPROVE THE PLANNING COMMISSION MINUTES OF NOVEMBER 5, 2018
  AS PRESENTED.

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  READING IN FULL OF ALL ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS PRESENTED FOR
  CONSIDERATION TO THE PLANNING COMMISSION WILL BE WAIVED AND ALL
  SUCH ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS WILL BE READ BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6-A

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered.

  B.  2018 SEMI-ANNUAL CODE COMPLIANCE REPORT

Planning Commission Meeting  1
Minutes, December 3, 2018
   COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER YOO to,

  APPROVE ITEM 6-B

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  NONE

  8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-21-18; APPLICANT: EXER MORE THAN URGENT
  CARE; LOCATION: 395 SILVER SPUR ROAD; A Conditional Use Permit is requested to
  operate an urgent care medical facility. A Precise Plan of Design is requested to replace
  existing sliding glass doors.

  Associate Planner Thom presented a summary of the staff report for Planning Application
  No. 21-18, a request for a Conditional Use Permit to operate an urgent care medical facility
  and a Precise Plan of Design to modify the building exterior. The project would include an
  interior remodel and changing the existing sliding glass doors. It is estimated that there
  will be an average of 50 patients per day and a total of 7 employees, however, during the
  peak flu season, those numbers may increase. Associate Planner Thom stated that the
  project site, Peninsula Center, has an existing parking variance for less than the minimum
  parking spaces required and it does not appear that this will intensify the use on the site.

  Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission,
  open the public hearing; take public testimony; discuss the issues; close the public hearing;
  and, adopt Resolution No. PA-21-18 approving the project.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the parking variance is for this building or the entire
  shopping center. Planning Director Wahba stated that a variance was approved for the
  entire center in 2014. COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his concern with the buildings
  drive-thru remaining and stated that the drive-thru should be removed to accommodate
  more parking. Planning Director Wahba stated that this has been discussed and can be
  made a conditional of approval for this project.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT expressed his concern with the number of urgent care facilities
  and the close vicinity between them within the City. Planning Director Wahba stated that
  there are other medical uses coming into the city including one in the same center and
  stated that this may be something that the City Council can review as a policy discussion
  at a later date.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that this site is different than compared to Deep Valley Drive
  where there are several medical uses and stated that that this is a prime retail space.
  CHAIR MEDAWAR stated that he would like to see a sales tax generating use at this site.

Planning Commission Meeting  2
Minutes, December 3, 2018
   CHAIR MEDAWAR asked if there will be an emergency pick-up and drop-off area and
  also agreed that he would like to see the drive-thru removed to accommodate more
  parking.

  COMMISSIONER YOO expressed his concern with emergency vehicles and how traffic
  will be impacted in the area.

  VICE CHAIR stated that typically emergency vehicles would not be coming and going from
  this type of facility. He also agrees that the drive-thru should be removed for more parking.

  COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated that in regards to the General Plan Update, the
  number of medical facilities in the city has not come up and suggested that this should be
  addressed and start to target what uses are met in the various areas.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked about other medical uses in the center. Planning Director
  Wahba stated that there are various medical uses in the center.

  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he does not mind another medical facility to keep
  people on the hill and would be in favor of the drive-thru area being removed.
  COMMISSIONER EDLER stated that he would like to see the city dictate a plan to get
  more parking into the whole center.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR opened the public hearing

  Noel Domingo and Sofya Lapina, Interior Designers for the Project, approached the
  podium. The Planning Commission had no questions.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR closed the public hearing

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked how the policy on medical uses could be brought to the
  attention of the City Council. Planning Director Wahba stated that this could be added to
  his agenda for the Policy Development Workshop in March and this could also be
  discussed as part of the General Plan Update on the commercial district.

  Discussion ensued on bringing this case before the City Council for policy direction prior
  to approval. Planning Director Wahba stated that this could be continued in order to get
  policy direction from the City Council as well as discuss with the applicant and property
  owner regarding eliminating the drive-thru area to allow for more parking.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR re-opened the public hearing

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT explained the concerns of the Planning Commission and asked
  about the timeline of the developer, Scott Whitney, Exer More Than Urgent Care, stated
  that they are in the process of submitting drawings for approval, once plans are approved,
  construction would begin within 90 days. The target date to open is June or July of 2019
  with construction beginning within the first quarter of 2019.

Planning Commission Meeting  3
Minutes, December 3, 2018
   Mr. Whitney stated that this business is growing and landlords support this use because
  it brings in a different mix of customers into their center. He stated that on the upper end
  of average, they see 50 patients a day and during flu season it could increase to 80 to 100
  patients per day. Mr. Whitney further explained the business model and also stated that
  they partner with local schools and provide charitable contributions.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCOTT, Mr. Whitney provided the number
  of existing and future locations.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER, Mr. Whitney stated that
  they will very rarely have ambulances to the facility and further explained that they are not
  set-up to receive patients by ambulance.

  Mr. Whitney stated that Vestar’s goal was to have this space occupied by a restaurant. He
  approached Jeff Axtel (Vestar) to consider allowing this use in the center and was offered
  a location further back in the shopping center, however, he explained that they are most
  successful in areas where there is more traffic flow. He stated that Mr. Axtel did not have
  a viable restaurant to put into the space and offered this space as an option, which is their
  ideal location.

  In response to a question by CHAIR MEDAWAR, Mr. Whitney stated that they have been
  looking for a location on the Peninsula for about a year.

  CHAIR MEDAWAR closed the public hearing.

  Further discussion was held on how to proceed with this item with an urgency for City
  Council to provide policy direction on future medical uses in the city.

  Per the request of the Planning Commission, Planning Director Wahba stated that he will
  alert the City Council in their weekly memo regarding the Planning Commission’s concerns
  with this project and the policy of medical uses coming to the Peninsula Shopping Center.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACTHER
  to,
  APPROVE RESOLUTION PA-21-18 SUBJECT TO THE CONDITION THAT, 1)
  VESTAR AGREE, WITHIN 1 YEAR, TO REMOVE THE DRIVE-THRU LANE AND
  REPLACE THAT AREA WITH PARKING; AND 2) THAT THIS SUBJECT BE
  HIGHLIGHTED IN THE WEEKLY MEMO AND THAT THE MINUTES HIGHLIGHT
  THE PLANNING COMMISSION’S POLICY CONCERNS.

  AYES:  Edler, Carman, Scott, Medawar, Zigrang, Schachter, Yoo
  NOES:
  ABSENT:
  ABSTAIN:

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

Planning Commission Meeting  4
Minutes, December 3, 2018
   9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  NONE

  10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

  A.  2019 PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING SCHEDULE

  Planning Director Wahba reminded the Planning Commission on the city’s “adopt-a-family”
  for the holidays. He also announced that the city’s annual Holiday Party will be held on
  December 13, 2018.

  Planning Director Wahba stated that there will be no meeting in January. The next
  Planning Commission meeting will be held on February 4, 2019, which will also be the
  time when the new Chair and Vice Chair will be announced as well as Committee
  assignments.

  11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, NOVEMBER 13, 2018

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS, NOVEMBER 27, 2018

  C.  DRAFT PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES, NOVEMBER 19,
  2018

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 11A – 11C

  There being no objection, CHAIR MEDAWAR so ordered

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR MEDAWAR adjourned the meeting at 8:11 p.m. to the next Planning
  Commission meeting on February 4, 2019.
